definition_en: waste material that is thrown away; things of poor quality; foolish talk or ideas
core_image: 一堆被丢弃、不再有用的东西
scene: 请把厨房里的垃圾拿出去。Please take the rubbish out of the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 rubbish 是「垃圾」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请把厨房里的垃圾拿出去。

senses.title: Waste material
senses.definition: waste material that is thrown away
senses.example: The bin was full of rubbish.
senses.exampleCN: 垃圾桶里装满了垃圾。
senses.why: The core sense is useless waste.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是无用的废弃物。

senses.title: Poor quality things
senses.definition: things that are of very poor quality
senses.example: The film was pure rubbish.
senses.exampleCN: 那部电影简直一无是处。
senses.why: Waste material becomes a judgment on things.
senses.whyCN: 废弃物变成了对事物的评价。

senses.title: Foolish talk
senses.definition: foolish talk or ideas
senses.example: Don't talk rubbish about her.
senses.exampleCN: 别乱说她的是非。
senses.why: Worthless things become worthless words.
senses.whyCN: 没有价值的东西变成没有价值的话。

intro.en: Rubbish comes from Middle English robous, rubble or waste.
intro.cn: rubbish 源自中古英语 robous，意为碎石、废料。

items.en: Robous names broken stone and waste.
items.cn: robous 指碎石与废料。

items.en: Related forms describe rubble from buildings.
items.cn: 相关词形描述建筑物产生的碎石。

items.en: Rubbish broadens to household waste.
items.cn: rubbish 扩大到家庭垃圾。

items.en: Rubbish also means worthless things.
items.cn: rubbish 也指毫无价值的东西。

items.en: Talk rubbish is a common phrase.
items.cn: talk rubbish 成为常用说法。

note.en: Rubbish is waste; rubble is broken stone.
note.cn: rubbish 是垃圾，rubble 则是碎砖石。

a soft material from tree sap

normalIntro.en: Rubbish is what is thrown out or has no worth.
normalIntro.cn: rubbish 是被扔掉或没有价值的东西。

normal.en: The street was covered in rubbish after the fair.
normal.cn: 集市过后街上到处是垃圾。

normal.en: That argument is complete rubbish.
normal.cn: 那个论点完全站不住脚。

normal.en: They collect rubbish every Tuesday morning.
normal.cn: 他们每周二早上收垃圾。

normal.en: He threw the old magazines into the rubbish.
normal.cn: 他把旧杂志扔进了垃圾里。

normal.en: Do not believe the rubbish in that message.
normal.cn: 别相信那条消息里的胡话。

abstract.en: Picture a bin overflowing at the curb.
abstract.cn: 想象路边一个满溢的垃圾桶。

abstract.en: Imagine torn paper blowing across a yard.
abstract.cn: 想象碎纸在院子里被风吹动。

abstract.en: Think of words that fall apart as you hear them.
abstract.cn: 想象一些话一听就站不住脚。

examples.en: The council collects household rubbish on Mondays.
examples.cn: 市政部门每周一收集生活垃圾。

examples.en: The film was dismissed as rubbish by critics.
examples.cn: 评论家斥那部电影为垃圾。

examples.en: He talks rubbish when he is nervous.
examples.cn: 他一紧张就胡说八道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rubbish」读起来像「垃圾堆里拉比什」，可以联想一袋被人丢弃的垃圾。

root: 中古英语 robous（碎石、废料）进入英语后扩展为「垃圾、废物、废话」。

sensesIntro.en: Rubbish means waste material, things of poor quality, or foolish talk.
sensesIntro.cn: rubbish 意为废弃物、劣质东西，或废话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heap of things thrown away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堆被丢弃的东西。

branches.en: The base sense is physical waste.
branches.cn: 基础义是实体的废弃物。

branches.en: Waste becomes a judgment of quality.
branches.cn: 废弃物变成对质量的判断。

branches.en: Worthless things become worthless words.
branches.cn: 无价值之物变成无价值之言。

branches.en: Physical and figurative waste share worthlessness.
branches.cn: 实体垃圾与比喻性垃圾都指没有价值。

branches.en: Bad products and bad talk are both dismissed.
branches.cn: 劣质产品与胡言乱语都会被否定。

intro.en: Rubbish is an old English word without a Latin root.
intro.cn: rubbish 是古老的英语词，没有拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Rubbish has no Latin root; it comes from Middle English.
latinIntro.cn: rubbish 没有拉丁词根，它来自中古英语。

items.example: Robous is the earliest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: robous 是最早有记载的形式。

items.example: Rubbish keeps the sense of waste.

items.exampleCN: rubbishy 形容廉价劣质的东西。

items.example: Bin forms the compound rubbish bin.
items.exampleCN: bin 构成复合词 rubbish bin。

items.example: Dump forms the compound rubbish dump.
items.exampleCN: dump 构成复合词 rubbish dump。

definition_en: not polite; offensive or insulting; roughly made or simple
core_image: 未经打磨的粗糙表面，欠缺应有的礼数
scene: 对服务员大喊大叫是很无礼的。Shouting at the waiter is very rude.
sceneCN: 这里 rude 是「无礼的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：对服务员大喊大叫是很无礼的。

senses.title: Not polite
senses.definition: not polite in behavior or speech
senses.example: It is rude to interrupt.
senses.exampleCN: 打断别人说话是不礼貌的。
senses.why: The core sense is a lack of polish.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是欠缺应有的修养。

senses.title: Offensive
senses.definition: offensive or insulting in an obvious way
senses.example: He made a rude gesture.
senses.exampleCN: 他做了个粗鲁的手势。
senses.why: Impoliteness hardens into open offence.
senses.whyCN: 不礼貌固化为公开冒犯。

senses.title: Roughly made
senses.definition: roughly made or simple in a primitive way
senses.definitionCN: 制作粗糙或原始简朴的
senses.example: They sheltered in a rude wooden hut.
senses.exampleCN: 他们躲在一间简陋的木屋里。
senses.why: The old sense is raw and unformed.
senses.whyCN: 旧义是未经加工、粗糙的。

intro.en: Rude comes from Latin rudis, raw and unformed.
intro.cn: rude 源自拉丁语 rudis，意为原始、未加工的。

items.en: Rudis means raw or rough.
items.cn: rudis 意为生的、粗糙的。

items.en: Rude keeps the sense of roughness.
items.cn: rude 保留粗糙的含义。

items.en: Rude describes rough work or manners.
items.cn: rude 形容粗糙的作品或举止。

items.en: Rude shifts toward social impoliteness.
items.cn: rude 转向指社交上的不礼貌。

items.en: Rude mainly means impolite today.
items.cn: 如今 rude 主要表示不礼貌。

note.en: Rude is impolite; crude is rough or unrefined.
note.cn: rude 是不礼貌，crude 则是粗制或粗俗。

entries.definition: a statement of what is allowed

normalIntro.en: Rude is unpolished, either in manners or in form.
normalIntro.cn: rude 是未经打磨，既指礼数也指做工。

normal.en: It is rude to point at people.
normal.cn: 用手指人是不礼貌的。

normal.en: She was rude to the driver for no reason.
normal.cn: 她无缘无故对司机无礼。

normal.en: The visitors made rude comments about the food.
normal.cn: 客人们对食物说了些粗鲁的话。

normal.en: They built a rude shelter from branches.
normal.cn: 他们用树枝搭了个简陋的棚子。

normal.en: His rude awakening came when the bill arrived.
normal.cn: 账单寄来时他才猛然醒悟。

abstract.en: Picture a rough stone never polished smooth.
abstract.cn: 想象一块从未打磨光滑的石头。

abstract.en: Imagine a door slammed in someone's face.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门当着人的面被摔上。

abstract.en: Think of a hut made from loose branches.
abstract.cn: 想象一间用松散树枝搭成的小屋。

examples.en: The clerk was rude to every customer.
examples.cn: 那名店员对每位顾客都很无礼。

examples.en: He apologized for his rude remarks.
examples.cn: 他为自己的无礼言论道歉。

examples.en: They slept in a rude hut near the river.
examples.cn: 他们睡在河边一间简陋的木屋里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rude」读音像「鲁的」：言行鲁莽无礼，就是「粗鲁的」。

root: 拉丁语 rudis（生的、未加工的）经古法语进入英语，核心义「未经打磨」，由物及人引申为「无礼」。

sensesIntro.en: Rude means impolite, openly offensive, or roughly and simply made.
sensesIntro.cn: rude 意为不礼貌的、公然冒犯的，或制作粗糙简朴的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough surface with no polish.
core.cn: 核心意象：没有打磨过的粗糙表面。

branches.en: The base sense is a lack of good manners.
branches.cn: 基础义是缺乏礼貌。

branches.en: Impoliteness becomes open offence.
branches.cn: 不礼貌变成公然冒犯。

branches.en: The old sense of roughness survives in objects.
branches.cn: 「粗糙」的旧义仍保留在物品上。

branches.en: Both concern behavior that harms others.
branches.cn: 两者都涉及伤害他人的行为。

branches.en: Unpolished manners and unpolished wood pair up.
branches.cn: 未修饰的举止与未打磨的木头相互对应。

intro.en: Rude comes from Latin rudis without a prefix.
intro.cn: rude 来自拉丁语 rudis，不带前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin rudis is the direct source of rude.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rudis 是 rude 的直接来源。

items.example: Rudis is the source of rude.
items.exampleCN: rudis 是 rude 的来源。

items.example: Rude keeps the sense of roughness.

definition_zh: 粗鲁地；无礼地；突然而粗暴地
definition_en: in an impolite way; in an offensive way; suddenly and roughly
core_image: 不打招呼就闯进来，动作又直又硬
scene: 他粗鲁地打断了我的解释。He rudely interrupted my explanation.
sceneCN: 这里 rudely 是「粗鲁地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他粗鲁地打断了我的解释。

senses.title: Impolite in manner
senses.definition: in a way that shows bad manners
senses.example: He rudely interrupted me.
senses.exampleCN: 他粗鲁地打断了我。
senses.why: The adverb describes impolite action.
senses.whyCN: 副词形式描述无礼的动作。

senses.title: Offensively
senses.definition: in a way that offends people
senses.example: She rudely pointed at my shoes.
senses.exampleCN: 她无礼地指着我的鞋子。
senses.why: Bad manners become open offence.
senses.whyCN: 不礼貌变成公开冒犯。

senses.title: Suddenly and roughly
senses.definition: suddenly and in a rough manner
senses.example: We were rudely awakened by the alarm.
senses.exampleCN: 我们被警报声猛然吵醒。
senses.why: Roughness applies to sudden events.
senses.whyCN: 「粗暴」也用于突如其来的事件。

intro.en: Rudely is rude plus the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: rudely 是 rude 加副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: Rudis means raw or rough.
items.cn: rudis 意为生的、粗糙的。

items.en: Rude keeps the sense of roughness.
items.cn: rude 保留粗糙的含义。

items.en: Rude describes rough manners.
items.cn: rude 形容粗鲁的举止。

items.en: -Ly turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.cn: -ly 把形容词变成副词。

items.en: Rudely covers manners and sudden events.
items.cn: rudely 既指礼数也指突然事件。

note.en: Rudely means impolitely; crudely means roughly or simply.
note.cn: rudely 是无礼地，crudely 则是粗糙地。

normalIntro.en: Rudely describes actions done without polish or courtesy.
normalIntro.cn: rudely 描述缺乏礼数、不加修饰的动作。

normal.en: He rudely pushed past the queue.
normal.cn: 他粗鲁地插队挤了过去。

normal.en: She rudely refused the invitation.
normal.cn: 她无礼地拒绝了邀请。

normal.en: Do not speak rudely to the staff.
normal.cn: 不要对员工说话无礼。

normal.en: We were rudely woken by hammering.
normal.cn: 我们被敲击声猛然吵醒。

normal.en: The question was rudely worded.
normal.cn: 这个问题的措辞很无礼。

abstract.en: Picture a door thrown open without a knock.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门没敲就被猛推开。

abstract.en: Imagine a voice cutting across a quiet room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音劈开安静的房间。

abstract.en: Think of an elbow pushing through a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手肘从人群中硬挤过去。

examples.en: The boy rudely answered back his teacher.
examples.cn: 那个男孩粗鲁地顶撞老师。

examples.en: They rudely ignored the old man's greeting.
examples.cn: 他们无礼地无视了老人的问候。

examples.en: The village was rudely shaken by the blast.
examples.cn: 爆炸猛然震动了整个村庄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rudely」是 rude（粗鲁的）加 -ly：以粗鲁的方式做事，就是「粗鲁地」。

root: 由 rude（粗鲁的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，rude 源自拉丁语 rudis（未加工的、粗糙的）。

sensesIntro.en: Rudely means impolitely, offensively, or suddenly and roughly.
sensesIntro.cn: rudely 意为不礼貌地、冒犯地，或突然而粗暴地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard, unpolished action.
core.cn: 核心意象：又硬又未经修饰的动作。

branches.en: The base sense is impolite action.
branches.cn: 基础义是不礼貌的行为。

branches.en: Impoliteness becomes open offence.
branches.cn: 不礼貌变成公开冒犯。

branches.en: Roughness describes sudden shocks.
branches.cn: 粗暴用于描述突然的冲击。

branches.en: Both describe behavior that hurts others.
branches.cn: 两者都描述伤害他人的行为。

branches.en: Bad manners and rough force share bluntness.
branches.cn: 无礼与粗暴共享「直接生硬」的特点。

intro.en: Rudely is rude plus the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: rudely 是 rude 加副词后缀 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin rudis lies behind the adjective rude.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rudis 是形容词 rude 的根源。

definition_en: a small carpet for a floor; a thick blanket; an informal word for a hairpiece
core_image: 一块铺在地上、质地厚实的织物
scene: 她床边铺着一块小小的羊毛地毯。A small wool rug lay beside her bed.
sceneCN: 这里 rug 是「小地毯」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她床边铺着一块小小的羊毛地毯。

senses.title: Small carpet
senses.definition: a small carpet used on a floor
senses.example: She laid a rug by the bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她在床边铺了一块小地毯。
senses.why: The core object is a small floor covering.
senses.whyCN: 核心物件是铺地的小块织物。

senses.title: Thick blanket
senses.definition: a thick blanket used for warmth
senses.example: He wrapped a wool rug around his shoulders.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一条羊毛厚毯披在肩上。
senses.why: The same coarse fabric serves as a wrap.
senses.whyCN: 同样的粗织物也可当披盖。

senses.title: Hairpiece
senses.definition: an informal word for a hairpiece
senses.example: Everyone noticed his new rug.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都注意到了他的新假发。
senses.why: A covering on a surface becomes a covering on the head.
senses.whyCN: 覆在表面的东西变成覆在头上的东西。

intro.en: Rug probably comes from a Scandinavian word for a coarse cover.
intro.cn: rug 可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语中表示粗毯的词。

items.en: Rugga names a rough, shaggy cover.
items.cn: rugga 指粗糙、毛茸茸的覆盖物。

items.en: Rugge means a coarse woollen cloth.
items.cn: rugge 意为粗毛织物。

items.en: Rug narrows to a floor covering.
items.cn: rug 收窄为铺地织物。

items.en: Rug also means a warm travelling blanket.
items.cn: rug 也指旅行用的保暖毯。

items.en: Rug gains the slang sense of a hairpiece.
items.cn: rug 获得「假发」的俚语义。

note.en: A rug covers the floor; a rag is a torn cloth.
note.cn: rug 铺在地上，rag 则是破布。

entries.definition: to move a hand over a surface
a small piece of material for the floor

normalIntro.en: A rug is a thick cover, usually on the floor.
normalIntro.cn: rug 是一块厚实的覆盖物，通常铺在地上。

normal.en: A red rug warmed the cold room.
normal.cn: 一块红地毯让冷屋子暖和起来。

normal.en: She shook the dust from the rug.
normal.cn: 她抖掉小地毯上的灰尘。

normal.en: He sat on a rug in front of the fire.
normal.cn: 他坐在炉火前的地毯上。

normal.en: The cat slept on the kitchen rug.
normal.cn: 猫睡在厨房的小地毯上。

normal.en: They spread a rug under the tree.
normal.cn: 他们在树下铺开一块毯子。

abstract.en: Picture a bright square warming a bare floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一块明亮的小方毯温暖光秃的地面。

abstract.en: Imagine coarse wool woven into a soft cover.
abstract.cn: 想象粗羊毛被织成柔软的覆盖物。

abstract.en: Think of a traveller wrapped against the cold.
abstract.cn: 想象旅人裹着毯子御寒。

examples.en: The rug in the hall is faded and worn.
examples.cn: 门厅里的地毯已经褪色磨损。

examples.en: He spread a rug on the grass for lunch.
examples.cn: 他在草地上铺了块毯子吃午饭。

examples.en: We bought a small rug for the bathroom.
examples.cn: 我们给浴室买了一块小地毯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rug」短促有力，像一块被铺平、踩在脚下的厚毯。

root: 可能源自斯堪的纳维亚语 rugga（粗毛覆盖物），经中古英语 rugge（粗毛织物）演变为「小地毯」。

sensesIntro.en: Rug means a small floor carpet, a thick blanket, or informally a hairpiece.
sensesIntro.cn: rug 意为小地毯、厚毯，或俚语中的假发。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick woven square on a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：铺在表面上的一块厚织物。

branches.en: The main sense is a small floor carpet.
branches.cn: 主要义是铺地的小地毯。

branches.en: The covering serves as a warm blanket.
branches.cn: 这种覆盖物也可当保暖毯。

branches.en: The idea of a cover extends to a hairpiece.
branches.cn: 「覆盖物」的概念扩展到假发。

branches.en: Both are thick woven covers people use.
branches.cn: 两者都是人们使用的厚织覆盖物。

branches.en: Floor cover and head cover share the shape idea.
branches.cn: 地面覆盖与头部覆盖共享「盖住」的概念。

intro.en: Rug is a short old word with compound partners.
intro.cn: rug 是个古老的短词，常与其他词构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Rug has no Latin root; it is of Scandinavian origin.
latinIntro.cn: rug 没有拉丁词根，源自斯堪的纳维亚语。

definition_en: to destroy or spoil something; to make someone bankrupt; the remains of a destroyed building
core_image: 原本立着的东西轰然倒塌，只剩残骸
scene: 一场暴雨毁掉了他们的婚礼。A heavy storm ruined their wedding.
sceneCN: 这里 ruin 是「毁掉」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一场暴雨毁掉了他们的婚礼。

senses.title: Destroy or spoil
senses.definition: to destroy or spoil something
senses.example: The rain ruined the picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨毁了野餐。
senses.why: The core sense is violent collapse.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是猛烈倒塌、毁掉。

senses.title: Make bankrupt
senses.definition: to make someone lose all their money or success
senses.definitionCN: 使某人失去全部钱财或前程
senses.example: The lawsuit ruined the family.
senses.exampleCN: 这场官司使这家人破产。
senses.why: Physical destruction extends to a person's life.
senses.whyCN: 物理毁坏扩展到人的生计。

senses.title: Remains of a building
senses.definition: the remains of a destroyed building
senses.example: We walked among the ruins.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在废墟间行走。
senses.why: The result of collapse is the ruin itself.
senses.whyCN: 倒塌的结果就是废墟本身。

intro.en: Ruin comes from Latin ruina, a falling down.
intro.cn: ruin 源自拉丁语 ruina，意为「倒塌」。

items.en: Ruere means to fall or rush down.
items.cn: ruere 意为坠落、冲下。

items.en: Ruina names a collapse or fallen mass.
items.cn: ruina 指倒塌或坍塌的堆积物。

items.en: Ruine keeps the sense of collapse.
items.cn: ruine 保留倒塌的含义。

items.en: Ruin covers both destruction and remains.
items.cn: ruin 兼指毁坏与残骸。

items.en: Ruin extends to money and reputation.
items.cn: ruin 扩展到金钱与名誉。

note.en: Ruin is to destroy; rain is falling water.
note.cn: ruin 是毁掉，rain 则是雨水。

entries.definition: a strap for controlling a horse

normalIntro.en: Ruin is a fall that leaves nothing whole.
normalIntro.cn: ruin 是一场留下残缺的倒塌。

normal.en: The floods ruined the harvest.
normal.cn: 洪水毁了收成。

normal.en: One bad deal ruined the small company.
normal.cn: 一笔糟糕的交易毁掉了这家小公司。

normal.en: The castle is now a romantic ruin.
normal.cn: 这座城堡如今是一片浪漫的废墟。

normal.en: Smoke ruined the curtains.
normal.cn: 烟把窗帘熏坏了。

normal.en: They explored the ruins of the old town.
normal.cn: 他们探访了古城的废墟。

abstract.en: Picture a tall wall cracking and falling.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵高墙开裂倒塌。

abstract.en: Imagine fine china dropped on a stone floor.
abstract.cn: 想象精美瓷器摔在石头地上。

abstract.en: Think of grass growing over broken stones.
abstract.cn: 想象荒草长满碎石。

examples.en: The scandal ruined his political career.
examples.cn: 这桩丑闻毁掉了他的政治生涯。

examples.en: Heavy rain ruined most of the crop.
examples.cn: 大雨毁掉了大部分庄稼。

examples.en: Tourists come to see the Roman ruins.
examples.cn: 游客们来参观古罗马废墟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ruin」读音像「如印」：灾难如烙印般留下残迹，就是「毁灭、废墟」。

root: 拉丁语 ruina（倒塌）来自 ruere（坠落、冲下），核心义「轰然倒下、只剩残骸」。

sensesIntro.en: Ruin means to destroy something, to make someone bankrupt, or the remains of a destroyed place.
sensesIntro.cn: ruin 意为毁坏某物、使某人破产，或被毁之地的废墟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something standing that crashes down.
core.cn: 核心意象：立着的东西轰然倒塌。

branches.en: The base sense is destroying or spoiling.
branches.cn: 基础义是毁坏或破坏。

branches.en: Destruction extends to a person's fortunes.
branches.cn: 毁坏扩展到个人生计。

branches.en: The result of collapse is the ruins.
branches.cn: 倒塌的结果就是废墟。

branches.en: Things and lives can both be ruined.
branches.cn: 物品与人生都可以被毁掉。

branches.en: The act of ruin leaves the ruins behind.
branches.cn: 毁坏的动作留下废墟。

intro.en: Ruin goes back to Latin ruere and ruina.
intro.cn: ruin 可追溯到拉丁语 ruere 与 ruina。

latinIntro.en: Latin ruere (to fall) and ruina (collapse) are the sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ruere（坠落）与 ruina（倒塌）是来源。

items.example: Ruin keeps the sense of collapse.

latinEntries.exampleCN: ruere 是表示坠落的动词。

definition_en: an official statement of what is allowed; control by a government or person; to govern; to decide officially
core_image: 一根笔直的尺子，划出能做与不能做的界线
scene: 学校对手机使用有严格的规定。The school has a strict rule about phones.
sceneCN: 这里 rule 是「规定、规则」（第 1 个义项）；句意：学校对手机使用有严格的规定。

senses.title: Official statement
senses.definition: an official statement of what is allowed or required
senses.definitionCN: 规定允许或要求什么的正式条文
senses.example: The first rule is to arrive on time.
senses.exampleCN: 第一条规则是准时到达。
senses.why: The core sense is a straight standard.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一条笔直的标准线。

senses.title: Control by a ruler
senses.definition: control by a government or a person
senses.example: The island was under foreign rule for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个岛曾被外国统治多年。
senses.why: A standard of behavior becomes control of people.
senses.whyCN: 行为标准变成对人的控制。

senses.title: To govern
senses.definition: to govern a country or group
senses.example: The queen ruled for forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 女王统治了四十年。
senses.why: The noun of control becomes the verb of controlling.
senses.whyCN: 控制的名词变成控制的动词。

senses.title: Decide officially
senses.definition: to decide an official question
senses.example: The judge ruled in her favor.
senses.exampleCN: 法官判她胜诉。
senses.why: Setting a standard becomes giving a verdict.
senses.whyCN: 设定标准变成作出裁决。

intro.en: Rule comes from Latin regula, a straight stick or standard.
intro.cn: rule 源自拉丁语 regula，意为直尺或标准。

items.en: Regula means a straight stick.
items.cn: regula 意为笔直的杆或尺。

items.en: Regere means to guide or keep straight.
items.cn: regere 意为引导、使笔直。

items.en: Riule means a rule or order.
items.cn: riu le 意为规则或命令。

items.en: Rule covers standards and government.
items.cn: rule 兼指标准与统治。

items.en: Rule also means to give a decision.
items.cn: rule 还表示作出裁定。

note.en: A rule is a standard; a ruse is a trick.
note.cn: rule 是规则，ruse 则是计谋。

entries.definition: a rule made by a government

normalIntro.en: A rule draws a line and keeps people inside it.
normalIntro.cn: rule 划出一条界线，把人约束在其中。

normal.en: The club has a rule against smoking.
normal.cn: 俱乐部有禁止吸烟的规定。

normal.en: The emperor ruled the land for many years.
normal.cn: 皇帝统治这片土地多年。

normal.en: The court ruled that the arrest was illegal.
normal.cn: 法院裁定这次逮捕不合法。

normal.en: As a rule, she walks to work.
normal.cn: 通常她步行上班。

normal.en: Doctors ruled out a broken bone.
normal.cn: 医生排除了骨折的可能。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler drawing one firm straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子画出一条笔直的线。

abstract.en: Imagine a crown placed over a map.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶王冠压在地图上。

abstract.en: Think of a judge's hammer setting a boundary.
abstract.cn: 想象法官的木槌划出边界。

examples.en: Every game needs clear rules.
examples.cn: 每项游戏都需要明确的规则。

examples.en: The small kingdom was ruled by one family.
examples.cn: 这个小王国由一个家族统治。

examples.en: The committee ruled that the plan could proceed.
examples.cn: 委员会裁定该计划可以继续。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rule」与 ruler（尺子）同源：用尺子划出界线，就是「规则」；拿着尺子管人，就是「统治」。

root: 拉丁语 regula（直尺、标准）来自 regere（使笔直、引导），核心义「划出直线、立下标准」，再引申为统治与裁定。

sensesIntro.en: Rule means a regulation, control by a government, to govern, or to decide officially.
sensesIntro.cn: rule 意为规则、统治、治理，或正式裁定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight stick drawing a limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根直尺划出界限。

branches.en: The base sense is a standard or regulation.
branches.cn: 基础义是标准或规则。

branches.en: A standard becomes control over people.
branches.cn: 标准变成对人的控制。

branches.en: Control becomes the verb to govern.
branches.cn: 控制变成表示统治的动词。

branches.en: Setting a standard becomes issuing a verdict.
branches.cn: 设定标准变成作出裁决。

branches.en: Rules guide both daily life and courts.
branches.cn: 规则既指导日常也指导法庭。

intro.en: Rule comes from Latin regula, a straight measure.
intro.cn: rule 来自拉丁语 regula，意为直尺。

latinIntro.en: Latin regula and regere supply the core forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 regula 与 regere 提供核心词形。

items.example: Regula is the direct source of rule.
items.exampleCN: regula 是 rule 的直接来源。

items.example: Regere gives the sense of guiding.

items.meaning: a measuring stick or a governor
items.example: Ruler adds the person or tool ending.
items.exampleCN: ruler 加上了表示人或工具的结尾。

latinEntries.exampleCN: regere 是表示引导的动词。

definition_en: a straight strip used for measuring and drawing lines; a person who governs a country; someone who controls a group
core_image: 一根笔直、带刻度的长条，或手持权杖发号施令的人
scene: 他用尺子画了一条笔直的线。He used a ruler to draw a straight line.
sceneCN: 这里 ruler 是「尺子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他用尺子画了一条笔直的线。

senses.title: Measuring strip
senses.definition: a straight strip used for measuring and drawing lines
senses.definitionCN: 用来测量和画线的直条
senses.example: Use a ruler to draw a straight line.
senses.exampleCN: 用尺子画一条直线。
senses.why: The core tool is a straight measure.
senses.whyCN: 核心工具是笔直的测量条。

senses.title: Person who governs
senses.definition: a person who governs a country
senses.example: The ruler of the small kingdom was kind.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小王国的统治者很仁慈。
senses.why: The straight standard becomes the person who sets it.
senses.whyCN: 画标准的人变成了设定标准的人。

senses.title: Controller of a group
senses.definition: someone who controls a group or situation
senses.definitionCN: 控制一个群体或局面的人
senses.example: She was the real ruler of the household.
senses.exampleCN: 她才是这个家真正的掌权者。
senses.why: Political control extends to daily life.
senses.whyCN: 政治上的控制扩展到日常生活。

intro.en: Ruler is rule plus the person suffix -er.
intro.cn: ruler 是 rule 加表示人的后缀 -er。

items.en: Regula means a straight stick.
items.cn: regula 意为直尺。

items.en: Riule keeps the sense of a standard.
items.cn: riu le 保留标准之义。

items.en: Rule covers measuring and governing.
items.cn: rule 兼指测量与统治。

items.en: -Er forms the person or tool noun.
items.cn: -er 构成表示人或工具的名词。

items.en: Ruler names both a stick and a governor.
items.cn: ruler 同时指尺子和统治者。

note.en: A ruler measures or governs; a rule is the standard itself.
note.cn: ruler 是尺子或统治者，rule 则是标准本身。

entries.definition: an official who governs a region

normalIntro.en: A ruler can be a straight measuring tool or a governing person.
normalIntro.cn: ruler 既可以是笔直的测量工具，也可以是治理者。

normal.en: The ruler on my desk is made of steel.
normal.cn: 我桌上的尺子是钢制的。

normal.en: The ruler ordered a new road to be built.
normal.cn: 统治者下令修建一条新路。

normal.en: Children use rulers to draw neat lines.
normal.cn: 孩子们用尺子画整齐的线。

normal.en: The old ruler was loved by the people.
normal.cn: 那位老君主受到人民爱戴。

normal.en: He is the ruler of the chess club.
normal.cn: 他是这个棋社的掌权者。

abstract.en: Picture a steel strip with numbered marks.
abstract.cn: 想象一根带刻度的钢条。

abstract.en: Imagine a crown resting on a map.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶王冠放在地图上。

abstract.en: Think of a hand holding both a pen and a staff.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手同时握着笔和权杖。

examples.en: The line was drawn without a ruler.
examples.cn: 这条线不是用尺子画的。

examples.en: The ruler promised lower taxes.
examples.cn: 统治者承诺降低税收。

examples.en: Each ruler of the region left a mark on the city.
examples.cn: 这个地区的每一位统治者都在城中留下印记。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ruler」是 rule（规则）加 -er：定规则的工具是「尺子」，定规则的人是「统治者」。

root: 由 rule（规则、直尺）加 -er 构成，rule 源自拉丁语 regula（直尺、标准）。

sensesIntro.en: Ruler means a measuring strip, a person who governs, or someone who controls a group.
sensesIntro.cn: ruler 意为测量用的直尺、治理国家的人，或控制群体的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight measure or the person behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔直的测量物，或设定标准的人。

branches.en: The base sense is the measuring tool.
branches.cn: 基础义是测量工具。

branches.en: The standard becomes a governing person.
branches.cn: 标准变成治理者。

branches.en: Political control extends to daily groups.
branches.cn: 政治控制扩展到日常群体。

branches.en: Tool and governor share the same old root.
branches.cn: 工具与统治者共享同一古老词根。

branches.en: A monarch and a household head both rule.
branches.cn: 君主与一家之主都在治理。

intro.en: Ruler is rule plus the agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: ruler 是 rule 加施事后缀 -er。

latinIntro.en: Latin regula is the root of rule and ruler.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 regula 是 rule 与 ruler 的词根。

items.example: Ruling comes from the verb rule.

definition_en: an unverified story spread from person to person; general talk about something; to spread something as gossip
core_image: 一句未经证实的话在人群里悄悄传开
scene: 关于公司裁员的谣言迅速传开。The rumour about job cuts spread quickly.
sceneCN: 这里 rumour 是「谣言、传闻」（第 1 个义项）；句意：关于公司裁员的谣言迅速传开。

senses.title: Unverified story
senses.definition: an unverified story spread from person to person
senses.definitionCN: 在人与人之间传播的未经证实的故事
senses.example: There is a rumour that the factory will close.
senses.exampleCN: 有传闻说工厂将要关闭。
senses.why: The core sense is talk without proof.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是没有证据的说法。

senses.title: General talk
senses.definition: general talk about something, often unkind
senses.definitionCN: 关于某事的普遍议论，常带恶意
senses.example: Rumour spread through the village.
senses.exampleCN: 流言在村里传开了。
senses.why: One story becomes a wave of talk.
senses.whyCN: 一个说法变成一片议论。

senses.title: To spread as gossip
senses.definition: to spread something as gossip
senses.example: He is rumoured to be leaving.
senses.exampleCN: 据传他要离开。
senses.why: The noun becomes the act of spreading talk.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成传播说法的动作。

intro.en: Rumour comes from Latin rumor, noise or common talk.
intro.cn: rumour 源自拉丁语 rumor，意为喧哗或众人议论。

items.en: Rumor means noise or common talk.
items.cn: rumor 意为喧哗或众人议论。

items.en: Rumour keeps the sense of talk.
items.cn: rumour 保留议论之义。

items.en: Rumour names unconfirmed news.
items.cn: rumour 指未经证实的消息。

items.en: The verb rumour appears in formal use.
items.cn: 动词 rumour 出现在正式用法中。

items.en: Rumour has it is a fixed phrase.
items.cn: rumour has it 成为固定说法。

note.en: A rumour is unproven talk; a report is a formal account.
note.cn: rumour 是未经证实的传言，report 则是正式报道。

entries.definition: a formal account of an event

normalIntro.en: A rumour is talk that travels before the facts.
normalIntro.cn: rumour 是跑在事实前面的说法。

normal.en: The rumour spread faster than the news.
normal.cn: 谣言的传播比新闻还快。

normal.en: She denied the rumour at once.
normal.cn: 她立刻否认了传闻。

normal.en: Rumour has it that the shop is closing.
normal.cn: 据传这家店要关门了。

normal.en: He is rumoured to have left the country.
normal.cn: 据传他已离开这个国家。

normal.en: Do not repeat a rumour you cannot prove.
normal.cn: 不要传播你无法证实的谣言。

abstract.en: Picture a whisper passing down a row of seats.
abstract.cn: 想象一句耳语沿着一排座位传下去。

abstract.en: Imagine a paper note folded and passed hand to hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸条被一只手传到另一只手。

abstract.en: Think of smoke that grows as it drifts.
abstract.cn: 想象烟越飘越浓。

examples.en: A rumour about the merger reached the press.
examples.cn: 关于合并的传闻传到了媒体那里。

examples.en: The rumour proved to be completely false.
examples.cn: 这个传闻被证明完全不实。

examples.en: It is rumoured that the coach will resign.
examples.cn: 据传教练将要辞职。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rumour」读音像「入耳」：一句话进到你耳朵里，却未必是真的，就是「谣言」。

root: 拉丁语 rumor（喧哗、众人议论）经古法语进入英语，核心义「没有确证却四处传播的说法」。

sensesIntro.en: Rumour means an unverified story, general talk, or to spread something as gossip.
sensesIntro.cn: rumour 意为未经证实的传闻、普遍议论，或把它当作流言传播。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whisper moving from ear to ear.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句耳语从一只耳朵传到另一只。

branches.en: The base sense is an unproven story.
branches.cn: 基础义是未经证实的故事。

branches.en: One story becomes a wave of talk.
branches.cn: 一个说法变成一片议论。

branches.en: The noun becomes the act of spreading talk.
branches.cn: 名词变成传播说法的动作。

branches.en: A single rumour feeds wider gossip.
branches.cn: 单个谣言喂养更广的流言。

branches.en: The story and spreading it are linked.
branches.cn: 传闻与传播它的动作相互关联。

intro.en: Rumour is a borrowing from Latin and Old French.
intro.cn: rumour 是从拉丁语和古法语借入的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin rumor, noise or talk, is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rumor（喧哗、议论）是直接来源。

items.exampleCN: rumoured 描述未经证实的消息。
spread 常与 rumour 搭配。

items.meaning: to say it is not true
items.exampleCN: deny 常与 rumour 搭配。

definition_en: to move quickly on foot; to operate or function; to manage a business; a period of activity
core_image: 脚步不停向前，机器不停转动
scene: 他每天清晨沿着河边跑步。He runs along the river every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 run 是「跑」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他每天清晨沿着河边跑步。

senses.title: Move fast on foot
senses.definition: to move quickly on foot
senses.example: She runs every morning before work.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天上班前都跑步。
senses.why: The core sense is fast forward motion.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是快速的向前运动。

senses.title: Operate
senses.definition: to operate or function
senses.example: The engine runs on diesel.
senses.exampleCN: 这台发动机靠柴油运转。
senses.why: Legs moving becomes a machine moving.
senses.whyCN: 双腿的跑动变成机器的运转。

senses.title: Manage
senses.definition: to manage or control a business
senses.example: He runs a small café near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他在车站附近经营一家小咖啡馆。
senses.why: Keeping something moving becomes managing it.
senses.whyCN: 让事物持续运转变成管理它。

senses.title: Period of activity
senses.definition: a period during which something operates or continues
senses.definitionCN: 某事运作或持续的时期
senses.example: The play had a long run in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这部戏在这座城市长期上演。
senses.why: The action becomes a stretch of time.
senses.whyCN: 动作变成一段时间。

intro.en: Run comes from Old English rinnan, to flow or run.
intro.cn: run 源自古英语 rinnan，意为流动、奔跑。

items.en: Rinnan means to flow or move quickly.
items.cn: rinnan 意为流动或快速移动。

items.en: Rinna reinforces the sense of flowing.
items.cn: rinna 强化了流动之义。

items.en: Runnen covers people, water, and machines.
items.cn: runnen 兼指人、水与机器。

items.en: Run extends to managing a business.
items.cn: run 扩展到经营企业。

items.en: In the long run becomes a fixed phrase.
items.cn: in the long run 成为固定搭配。

note.en: Run is fast movement; ruin is destruction.
note.cn: run 是快速移动，ruin 则是毁灭。

entries.definition: a strap for controlling a horse
to run very fast for a short distance
to work or make something work
to control a business or group

normalIntro.en: Run is anything moving onward without stopping.
normalIntro.cn: run 是任何持续向前运转的事物。

normal.en: The children ran across the field.
normal.cn: 孩子们跑过田野。

normal.en: The machine runs all night.
normal.cn: 机器整夜运转。

normal.en: She runs a bookshop on the corner.
normal.cn: 她在街角经营一家书店。

normal.en: We ran out of milk this morning.
normal.cn: 今天早上我们的牛奶用完了。

normal.en: The show had a successful run.
normal.cn: 这部演出连续上演很成功。

abstract.en: Picture feet hitting the ground in rhythm.
abstract.cn: 想象双脚有节奏地踏地。

abstract.en: Imagine wheels turning without pause.
abstract.cn: 想象车轮不停转动。

abstract.en: Think of a river flowing past a town.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河从城镇旁流过。

examples.en: He ran to catch the last bus.
examples.cn: 他跑去赶末班车。

examples.en: The factory runs day and night.
examples.cn: 这家工厂昼夜运转。

examples.en: They run a farm outside the city.
examples.cn: 他们在城外经营一座农场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「run」读音短促，像脚步快速点地：跑起来，机器也跟着转起来。

root: 古英语 rinnan（流动、奔跑）经中古英语 runnen 演变为「跑、运转、经营」，核心义「持续向前」。

sensesIntro.en: Run means to move fast on foot, to operate, to manage, or a period of activity.
sensesIntro.cn: run 意为奔跑、运转、经营，或一段活动时期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steady forward motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：持续向前的运动。

branches.en: The base sense is fast movement on foot.
branches.cn: 基础义是快速跑动。

branches.en: Human running becomes machine operation.
branches.cn: 人的跑动变成机器运转。

branches.en: Keeping things moving becomes managing.
branches.cn: 让事物运转变成经营管理。

branches.en: The action becomes a stretch of time.
branches.cn: 动作变成一段时间。

branches.en: Machines and businesses both keep running.
branches.cn: 机器与企业都需要持续运转。

intro.en: Run is an Old English verb with many related forms.
intro.cn: run 是古英语动词，衍生形式很多。

latinIntro.en: Run has no Latin root; it is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: run 没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语族。

items.exampleCN: runs 是现在时单数形式。

definition_en: a person who runs; a person taking part in a race; someone who carries goods illegally
core_image: 一双不停向前迈步的腿
scene: 这名跑者在最后一圈超过了所有人。The runner passed everyone on the final lap.
sceneCN: 这里 runner 是「赛跑者」（第 2 个义项）；句意：这名跑者在最后一圈超过了所有人。

senses.title: Person who runs
senses.definition: a person who runs
senses.example: A runner passed us on the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 一个跑步的人在山坡上超过了我们。
senses.why: The base sense adds a person to run.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是在 run 后加上人。

senses.title: Race competitor
senses.definition: a person taking part in a race
senses.example: The runner finished second.
senses.exampleCN: 这位赛跑者获得了第二。
senses.why: Running becomes an organized contest.
senses.whyCN: 跑步变成有组织的比赛。

senses.title: Illegal courier
senses.definition: someone who carries goods illegally
senses.example: Police stopped a drug runner at the border.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在边境拦下了一名毒品走私者。
senses.why: Carrying things quickly becomes smuggling.
senses.whyCN: 快速运送东西变成走私。

intro.en: Runner is run plus the person suffix -er.
intro.cn: runner 是 run 加表示人的后缀 -er。

items.en: Rinnan means to flow or run.
items.cn: rinnan 意为流动或奔跑。

items.en: Runnen covers people and water.
items.cn: runnen 兼指人与水。

items.en: -Er forms the person who runs.
items.cn: -er 构成跑步的人。

items.en: Runner also names a race competitor.
items.cn: runner 也指赛跑选手。

items.en: Runner extends to illegal couriers.
items.cn: runner 扩展到非法运送者。

note.en: A runner runs; a ruler measures or governs.
note.cn: runner 是跑步的人，ruler 则是尺子或统治者。

entries.definition: someone who runs slowly for exercise
someone who carries messages or goods

normalIntro.en: A runner is a person whose job or sport is running.
normalIntro.cn: runner 是以跑步为运动或职业的人。

normal.en: The runner trained for the city race.
normal.cn: 这名跑者为城市赛跑训练。

normal.en: A tired runner stopped at the water station.
normal.cn: 一名疲惫的跑者在补水站停下。

normal.en: She is the fastest runner in her class.
normal.cn: 她是班上跑得最快的人。

normal.en: The runner-up received a silver medal.
normal.cn: 亚军获得了一枚银牌。

normal.en: The police caught the runner at the port.
normal.cn: 警方在港口抓住了那名走私者。

abstract.en: Picture legs moving in a steady rhythm.
abstract.cn: 想象双腿以稳定节奏迈动。

abstract.en: Imagine a number on a runner's chest.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者胸前别着号码布。

abstract.en: Think of a parcel passed quickly in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一个包裹在暗处被快速传递。

examples.en: The runner broke the record by two seconds.
examples.cn: 这名赛跑者以两秒之差打破了纪录。

examples.en: A runner delivered the message before dawn.
examples.cn: 一名信使在黎明前送出了消息。

examples.en: Runners gathered at the start line.
examples.cn: 跑者们聚集在起跑线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「runner」是 run（跑）加 -er：不停跑动的人，就是「跑步者、赛跑者」。

root: 由 run（跑）加施事后缀 -er 构成，run 源自古英语 rinnan（流动、奔跑）。

sensesIntro.en: Runner means a person who runs, a race competitor, or someone who carries goods illegally.
sensesIntro.cn: runner 意为跑步的人、赛跑选手，或非法运送货物的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person in constant forward motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个持续向前奔跑的人。

branches.en: The base sense is a person who runs.
branches.cn: 基础义是跑步的人。

branches.en: Running becomes an organized race.
branches.cn: 跑步变成有组织的比赛。

branches.en: Fast carrying becomes smuggling.
branches.cn: 快速运送变成走私。

branches.en: Every racer is first a runner.
branches.cn: 每位赛跑者首先都是跑步的人。

branches.en: Race and illegal delivery both involve speed.
branches.cn: 赛跑与非法运送都强调速度。

intro.en: Runner is run plus the agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: runner 是 run 加施事后缀 -er。

latinIntro.en: Runner has no Latin root; run is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: runner 没有拉丁词根，run 属于日耳曼语族。

definition_en: relating to the countryside; typical of country life; based on farming and land
core_image: 一片开阔的田野、村庄和乡间小路
scene: 他们从城市搬到了乡下。They moved from the city to a rural area.
sceneCN: 这里 rural 是「乡下的、农村的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们从城市搬到了乡下。

senses.title: Of the countryside
senses.definition: relating to the countryside rather than towns
senses.definitionCN: 与乡村而非城镇有关的
senses.example: The clinic serves a large rural area.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为大片农村地区服务。
senses.why: The core sense is open country.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是开阔的乡野。

senses.title: Country life
senses.definition: typical of life in the countryside
senses.example: The village still has a rural charm.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄仍保留着田园魅力。
senses.why: Place becomes a style of life.
senses.whyCN: 地点变成一种生活方式。

senses.title: Farming based
senses.definition: based on farming and land work
senses.definitionCN: 以耕作和土地劳动为基础的
senses.example: Rural employment depends on farming.
senses.exampleCN: 农村就业依赖农业。
senses.why: Country life is tied to working the land.
senses.whyCN: 乡村生活与土地劳作紧密相连。

intro.en: Rural comes from Latin ruralis, from rus, open country.
intro.cn: rural 源自拉丁语 ruralis，来自 rus（开阔的乡野）。

items.en: Rus means open land or countryside.
items.cn: rus 意为开阔的土地或乡野。

items.en: Ruralis means of the countryside.
items.cn: ruralis 意为乡野的。

items.en: Rural keeps the country sense.
items.cn: rural 保留乡村之义。

items.en: Rural contrasts with urban.
items.cn: rural 与 urban 相对。

items.en: Rural development is a common phrase.
items.cn: rural development 成为常用搭配。

note.en: Rural means country; royal means kingly.
note.cn: rural 是乡村的，royal 则是王室的。

entries.definition: relating to a king or queen
using the basic meaning of words

normalIntro.en: Rural describes fields, villages, and country life.
normalIntro.cn: rural 描述田野、村庄与乡村生活。

normal.en: The rural road was quiet at dusk.
normal.cn: 傍晚的乡间小路很安静。

normal.en: Many young people leave rural towns for work.
normal.cn: 许多年轻人离开乡村去谋生。

normal.en: A rural school may have only a few pupils.
normal.cn: 乡村学校可能只有几个学生。

normal.en: The family enjoys a rural way of life.
normal.cn: 这家人喜欢乡村生活方式。

normal.en: Rural areas often lack fast internet.
normal.cn: 农村地区常常缺乏高速网络。

abstract.en: Picture a wide field under a low sky.
abstract.cn: 想象低垂天空下的一片广阔田野。

abstract.en: Imagine a lane bordered by hedges.
abstract.cn: 想象一条两旁是树篱的小路。

abstract.en: Think of a village bell heard far away.
abstract.cn: 想象远处传来的村庄钟声。

examples.en: The doctor travels between several rural villages.
examples.cn: 这位医生往返于几个乡村之间。

examples.en: Rural life can feel slow and peaceful.
examples.cn: 乡村生活可能显得缓慢而宁静。

examples.en: The government funds rural schools.
examples.cn: 政府为农村学校提供资金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rural」里有 rur，联想「入乡」：走进乡野，就是「乡村的、田园的」。

root: 拉丁语 rus（开阔乡野）的形容词 ruralis 进入英语，核心义「属于乡村与土地的」。

sensesIntro.en: Rural means relating to the countryside, typical of country life, or based on farming.
sensesIntro.cn: rural 意为与乡村有关的、具有乡村生活特征的，或以农业为基础的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: open fields and small villages.
core.cn: 核心意象：开阔田野与小村庄。

branches.en: The base sense is belonging to the country.
branches.cn: 基础义是属于乡村。

branches.en: Place becomes a way of living.
branches.cn: 地点变成一种生活方式。

branches.en: Country life is tied to farming.
branches.cn: 乡村生活与农业相连。

branches.en: Landscape and daily life go together.
branches.cn: 景观与日常生活相伴。

branches.en: Country style and farm work overlap.
branches.cn: 乡村风格与农活相互重叠。

intro.en: Rural comes from Latin rus with the adjective ending -alis.
intro.cn: rural 来自拉丁语 rus，并带形容词词尾 -alis。

latinIntro.en: Latin rus (country) and ruralis are the source forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rus（乡村）与 ruralis 是来源词形。

items.example: Rus is the source of rural.
items.exampleCN: rus 是 rural 的来源。

definition_en: to move quickly; to do something too fast; a sudden attack; a busy period
core_image: 人群或水流一下子朝一个方向猛冲
scene: 她抓起包就冲出了门。She grabbed her bag and rushed out of the door.
sceneCN: 这里 rush 是「冲」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她抓起包就冲出了门。

senses.title: Move quickly
senses.definition: to move with great speed
senses.example: She rushed to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她冲向车站。
senses.why: The core sense is sudden fast motion.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是突然的快速运动。

senses.title: Do too fast
senses.definition: to do something too quickly
senses.example: Don't rush the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 不要仓促作决定。
senses.why: Fast motion becomes hasty action.
senses.whyCN: 快速移动变成草率行事。

senses.title: Sudden attack
senses.definition: a sudden military attack
senses.example: The soldiers rushed the gate at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们在黎明时冲向大门。
senses.why: Charging forward becomes an assault.
senses.whyCN: 向前冲变成进攻。

senses.title: Busy period
senses.definition: a busy period when many people move
senses.definitionCN: 许多人同时涌动的繁忙时段
senses.example: The morning rush fills every train.
senses.exampleCN: 早高峰让每列火车都挤满人。
senses.why: The movement becomes a crowded time.
senses.whyCN: 运动变成拥挤的时段。

intro.en: Rush comes from Old French ruser, to drive back or charge.
intro.cn: rush 源自古法语 ruser，意为击退、猛冲。

items.en: Ruser means to drive back or push.
items.cn: ruser 意为击退或推挤。

items.en: Russher means to charge forward.
items.cn: russher 意为向前猛冲。

items.en: Rushen covers people and water.
items.cn: rushen 兼指人与水流。

items.en: Rush extends to hasty action.
items.cn: rush 扩展到仓促行事。

items.en: Rush hour names the busiest travel time.
items.cn: rush hour 指最繁忙的通行时段。

note.en: Rush is fast movement; rust is a red coat on iron.
note.cn: rush 是快速冲撞，rust 则是铁上的锈。

normalIntro.en: Rush is speed with little time to think.
normalIntro.cn: rush 是快得来不及思考的速度。

normal.en: People rush for the last train.
normal.cn: 人们冲向末班车。

normal.en: Do not rush your homework.
normal.cn: 不要急着赶作业。

normal.en: The water rushed over the rocks.
normal.cn: 水从岩石上冲过。

normal.en: The rush hour starts at five.
normal.cn: 高峰时段五点开始。

normal.en: They rushed through lunch to catch the bus.
normal.cn: 他们匆匆吃完午饭去赶公交。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd pouring through a narrow gate.
abstract.cn: 想象人群从窄门涌出。

abstract.en: Imagine a river after heavy rain.
abstract.cn: 想象暴雨后的河水。

abstract.en: Think of a clock hand moving too fast.
abstract.cn: 想象钟表的指针转得太快。

examples.en: The crowd rushed toward the open doors.
examples.cn: 人群朝敞开的大门冲去。

examples.en: He rushed his speech and made mistakes.
examples.cn: 他讲得太仓促，出了错。

examples.en: The morning rush makes the roads slow.
examples.cn: 早高峰让道路变得缓慢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rush」读音像「如射」：像箭一样射出去，就是「冲、匆忙」。

root: 源自古法语 ruser（击退、推挤），核心义「猛然向前冲」，再引申为仓促行事与高峰时段。

sensesIntro.en: Rush means to move fast, to act too quickly, a sudden attack, or a busy period.
sensesIntro.cn: rush 意为猛冲、仓促行事、突袭，或繁忙高峰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sudden surge toward something.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股力量突然涌向某处。

branches.en: The base sense is fast movement.
branches.cn: 基础义是快速移动。

branches.en: Fast movement becomes hasty action.
branches.cn: 快速移动变成仓促行事。

branches.en: Charging becomes a military attack.
branches.cn: 向前冲变成军事突袭。

branches.en: Movement becomes a crowded time.
branches.cn: 运动变成拥挤时段。

branches.en: The daily rush is many people moving fast.
branches.cn: 日常高峰就是许多人同时快速移动。

intro.en: Rush is a borrowing from Old French.
intro.cn: rush 是从古法语借入的词。

latinIntro.en: Rush has no direct Latin root in English use.
latinIntro.cn: rush 在英语用法中没有直接拉丁词根。

items.example: Ruser is the source of rush.
items.exampleCN: ruser 是 rush 的来源。
rushed 描述仓促完成的工作。

definition_en: a reddish coating that forms on iron; a plant disease; to become covered with rust
core_image: 铁表面慢慢爬满一层红褐色粉末
scene: 雨水让旧铁门生满了锈。Rain left the old iron gate covered in rust.
sceneCN: 这里 rust 是「铁锈」（第 1 个义项）；句意：雨水让旧铁门生满了锈。

senses.title: Iron coating
senses.definition: a reddish coating that forms on iron
senses.definitionCN: 铁表面形成的红褐色覆盖层
senses.example: The gate was covered in rust.
senses.exampleCN: 大门上布满了锈。
senses.why: The core sense is corroded iron.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是受腐蚀的铁面。

senses.title: Plant disease
senses.definition: a disease that leaves reddish spots on plants
senses.definitionCN: 在植物上留下红色斑点的病害
senses.example: Rust damaged the wheat crop.
senses.exampleCN: 锈病损害了小麦收成。
senses.why: The colour and spread are applied to plants.
senses.whyCN: 颜色与蔓延的特征被用于植物。

senses.title: To corrode
senses.definition: to become covered with rust
senses.example: The old car has rusted away.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆旧车已经锈蚀掉了。
senses.why: The noun becomes the process.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成生锈的过程。

intro.en: Rust comes from Old English rust, linked to the colour red.
intro.cn: rust 源自古英语 rust，与红色有关。

items.en: Rust names the red coat on iron.
items.cn: rust 指铁上的红色覆盖层。

items.en: Related words link rust with redness.
items.cn: 相关词把 rust 与红色联系起来。

items.en: Rust also names a plant disease.
items.cn: rust 也指一种植物病害。

items.en: Rust becomes a verb for corroding.
items.cn: rust 成为表示生锈的动词。

items.en: Rustproof is a common technical word.
items.cn: rustproof 成为常见技术词。

note.en: Rust is iron corrosion; dust is dry powder.
note.cn: rust 是铁锈，dust 则是灰尘。

normalIntro.en: Rust is what iron becomes when air and water win.
normalIntro.cn: rust 是空气和水战胜铁之后的产物。

normal.en: A patch of rust spread across the roof.
normal.cn: 一块锈斑在屋顶上蔓延。

normal.en: The chain rusted solid in the rain.
normal.cn: 铁链在雨中生锈卡死了。

normal.en: They painted the fence to stop rust.
normal.cn: 他们给栅栏刷漆防锈。

normal.en: Rust ruined the old tools in the shed.
normal.cn: 锈毁了棚子里的旧工具。

normal.en: This metal is treated to resist rust.
normal.cn: 这种金属经过处理以抗锈。

abstract.en: Picture red flakes spreading over grey iron.
abstract.cn: 想象红色薄片在灰铁上蔓延。

abstract.en: Imagine a lock slowly refusing to turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锁慢慢转不动了。

abstract.en: Think of time quietly eating metal.
abstract.cn: 想象时间悄悄侵蚀金属。

examples.en: Salt air makes the metal rust faster.
examples.cn: 含盐的空气使金属生锈更快。

examples.en: The old pipes were badly rusted.
examples.cn: 旧管道锈得很厉害。

examples.en: Rust had eaten through the thin sheet.
examples.cn: 锈已经蚀穿了薄板。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rust」读音短而硬，像铁表面粗糙的红锈；可联想「铁锈让东西生锈」。

root: 古英语 rust（铁上的红色覆盖层）与日耳曼语中表示红色的词同源，核心义「铁被侵蚀后的红褐色产物」。

sensesIntro.en: Rust means the red coating on iron, a plant disease, or to become corroded.
sensesIntro.cn: rust 意为铁锈、一种植物锈病，或生锈腐蚀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: red flakes eating into iron.
core.cn: 核心意象：红色薄片侵蚀铁面。

branches.en: The base sense is the coating on iron.
branches.cn: 基础义是铁上的锈层。

branches.en: The colour and spread apply to plants.
branches.cn: 颜色与蔓延特征用于植物。

branches.en: The noun becomes the corroding process.
branches.cn: 名词变成腐蚀过程。

branches.en: The coating is the result of the process.
branches.cn: 锈层是腐蚀过程的结果。

branches.en: Metal rust and plant rust share red spots.
branches.cn: 金属锈与植物锈病都有红色斑点。

intro.en: Rust is an Old English word with many compounds.
intro.cn: rust 是古英语词，复合形式很多。

latinIntro.en: Rust has no Latin root; it is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: rust 没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语族。

items.exampleCN: rusty 描述受腐蚀的金属。
rustproof 描述经过处理的金属。

definition_en: a large bag; an informal word for dismissal from a job; to dismiss someone; to plunder a town
core_image: 一只鼓鼓的大麻袋，或被人一把清空
scene: 他扛着一袋土豆走进厨房。He carried a sack of potatoes into the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 sack 是「麻袋、大袋」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他扛着一袋土豆走进厨房。

senses.title: Large bag
senses.definition: a large bag made of strong material
senses.definitionCN: 用结实材料制成的大袋子
senses.example: The farmer filled a sack with grain.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫把一袋谷物装满。
senses.why: The core object is a big bag.
senses.whyCN: 核心物件是大袋子。

senses.title: Dismissal
senses.definition: an informal word for being dismissed from a job
senses.example: She got the sack for being late.
senses.exampleCN: 她因迟到被解雇了。
senses.why: Being sent away with your bag becomes dismissal.
senses.whyCN: 带着袋子被赶走变成了解雇。

senses.title: To dismiss
senses.definition: to dismiss someone from a job
senses.example: They sacked the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 他们解雇了经理。
senses.why: The noun becomes the action.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动作。

senses.title: To plunder
senses.definition: to steal everything from a captured town
senses.definitionCN: 从被攻占的城镇抢走一切
senses.example: The soldiers sacked the city.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们洗劫了这座城市。
senses.why: Emptying a place is like emptying a sack.
senses.whyCN: 清空一座城就像倒空一只袋子。

intro.en: Sack has two origins: a Latin bag and a French word for plunder.
intro.cn: sack 有两个来源：拉丁语的袋子和法语中表示劫掠的词。

items.en: Saccus means a bag.
items.cn: saccus 意为袋子。

items.en: Sakkos names a coarse bag.
items.cn: sakkos 指粗布袋。

items.en: Sac means plunder or pillage.
items.cn: sac 意为劫掠。

items.en: Sak covers both bag and plunder.
items.cn: sak 兼指袋子与劫掠。

items.en: The sack comes to mean dismissal.
items.cn: the sack 引申为解雇。

note.en: A sack is a bag; to sock is to hit.
note.cn: sack 是袋子，sock 作动词则是猛击。

entries.definition: to remove someone from a job

normalIntro.en: A sack holds goods, and to sack is to empty a place.
normalIntro.cn: sack 能装东西，而 to sack 是把一个地方清空。

normal.en: He bought a sack of rice at the market.
normal.cn: 他在市场上买了一袋米。

normal.en: The worker was given the sack without notice.
normal.cn: 那名工人没被通知就被解雇了。

normal.en: The club sacked its coach after the loss.
normal.cn: 输球后俱乐部解雇了教练。

normal.en: The invaders sacked the town and burned it.
normal.cn: 入侵者洗劫并烧毁了小镇。

normal.en: She carried the sack on her shoulder.
normal.cn: 她把袋子扛在肩上。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy bag tied at the top.
abstract.cn: 想象一只扎紧口子的沉重袋子。

abstract.en: Imagine a desk cleared in one sweep.
abstract.cn: 想象桌子一下被清空。

abstract.en: Think of a town stripped bare.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城被抢得空空如也。

examples.en: They loaded the sacks onto the truck.
examples.cn: 他们把麻袋装上卡车。

examples.en: The coach was sacked after a poor season.
examples.cn: 赛季表现不佳后教练被解雇。

examples.en: The army sacked the old capital.
examples.cn: 军队洗劫了旧都。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sack」读音像「塞克」：把东西往袋子里塞，就是「麻袋」；把人塞出门，就是「解雇」。

root: 袋子义来自拉丁语 saccus（袋），劫掠义来自古法语 sac，两条词源进入英语后合成今天的 sack。

sensesIntro.en: Sack means a large bag, dismissal, to dismiss, or to plunder a place.
sensesIntro.cn: sack 意为大袋、解雇、解雇某人，或洗劫某地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a big bag, or a place emptied out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只大袋子，或被清空的地方。

branches.en: The base sense is a large bag.
branches.cn: 基础义是大袋子。

branches.en: Being sent off with your bag becomes dismissal.
branches.cn: 带着袋子被赶走变成解雇。

branches.en: The noun becomes the act of dismissing.
branches.cn: 名词变成解雇的动作。

branches.en: Emptying a place becomes plunder.
branches.cn: 清空一个地方变成劫掠。

branches.en: Dismissal as a noun and verb pair up.
branches.cn: 解雇的名词与动词相互对应。

intro.en: Sack comes from two sources and builds several compounds.
intro.cn: sack 有两个来源，并构成多个复合词。

latinIntro.en: The bag sense goes back to Latin saccus.
latinIntro.cn: 「袋子」义可追溯到拉丁语 saccus。

definition_en: to give up something valuable; to offer something to a god; the thing given up or offered
core_image: 把珍贵的东西郑重地放上祭台
scene: 父母为孩子牺牲了很多个人时间。The parents sacrificed a lot of personal time for their children.
sceneCN: 这里 sacrifice 是「牺牲、放弃」（第 1 个义项）；句意：父母为孩子牺牲了很多个人时间。

senses.title: Give up something
senses.definition: to give up something valuable for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为了某个目的放弃有价值的东西
senses.example: She sacrificed her career for the family.
senses.exampleCN: 她为了家庭放弃了自己的事业。
senses.why: The core sense is giving up something valued.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是放弃珍视之物。

senses.title: Offer to a god
senses.definition: to offer something to a god in a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 在仪式中把某物献给神
senses.example: They sacrificed a goat at the temple.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在神庙献祭了一只山羊。
senses.why: Giving up becomes a sacred offering.
senses.whyCN: 放弃变成神圣的奉献。

senses.title: The cost borne
senses.definition: the thing given up for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某个目的而放弃的东西
senses.example: The plan required great sacrifice.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划需要巨大牺牲。
senses.why: The act becomes the cost itself.
senses.whyCN: 动作变成所承受的代价。

intro.en: Sacrifice comes from Latin sacrificium, a sacred offering.
intro.cn: sacrifice 源自拉丁语 sacrificium，意为神圣的供奉。

items.en: Sacer means holy or sacred.
items.cn: sacer 意为神圣的。

items.en: Facere means to make or do.
items.cn: facere 意为制作、做。

items.en: Sacrificium joins holy and making.
items.cn: sacrificium 把「神圣」与「做」结合。

items.en: Sacrifice keeps the offering sense.
items.cn: sacrifice 保留供奉之义。

items.en: Sacrifice covers both rite and cost.
items.cn: sacrifice 兼指仪式与代价。

items.en: Personal sacrifice becomes common usage.
items.cn: personal sacrifice 成为常见说法。

note.en: Sacrifice is giving up; to suffice is to be enough.
note.cn: sacrifice 是放弃，suffice 则是足够。

normalIntro.en: Sacrifice is giving up something precious for something more important.
normalIntro.cn: sacrifice 是为更重要的东西放弃珍贵之物。

normal.en: Many parents sacrifice their own comfort.
normal.cn: 许多父母牺牲自己的舒适。

normal.en: The villagers sacrificed food at the harvest.
normal.cn: 村民在收获时献上食物。

normal.en: Victory came at a heavy sacrifice.
normal.cn: 胜利以沉重牺牲为代价。

normal.en: He sacrificed sleep to finish the work.
normal.cn: 他为完成工作牺牲了睡眠。

normal.en: The team made great sacrifices for the project.
normal.cn: 团队为这个项目作出了巨大牺牲。

abstract.en: Picture a prized object laid on a stone altar.
abstract.cn: 想象一件珍贵之物被放在石祭台上。

abstract.en: Imagine letting go of something you love.
abstract.cn: 想象放开你喜爱的东西。

abstract.en: Think of a candle burning itself to give light.
abstract.cn: 想象蜡烛燃烧自己照亮别人。

examples.en: She sacrificed her free time to help the club.
examples.cn: 她牺牲空闲时间来帮助俱乐部。

examples.en: The ancient rite involved a sacrifice.
examples.cn: 这种古老仪式包含献祭。

examples.en: Success here demands real sacrifice.
examples.cn: 在这里取得成功需要真正的牺牲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sacrifice」里有 sacri（神圣）：把珍贵的东西献给更重要的目标，就是「牺牲、献祭」。

root: 拉丁语 sacrificium 由 sacer（神圣的）与 facere（做）构成，核心义「做神圣之事、献上供物」。

sensesIntro.en: Sacrifice means to give something up, to offer it to a god, or the cost that is borne.
sensesIntro.cn: sacrifice 意为放弃某物、向神献祭，或所承受的代价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something precious placed on an altar.
core.cn: 核心意象：珍贵之物被放上祭台。

branches.en: The base sense is giving up something valued.
branches.cn: 基础义是放弃珍视之物。

branches.en: Giving up becomes a sacred offering.
branches.cn: 放弃变成神圣供奉。

branches.en: The act becomes the cost borne.
branches.cn: 动作变成承受的代价。

branches.en: What you give up is the cost.
branches.cn: 你所放弃的正是代价。

branches.en: Everyday loss and ritual offering share the act.
branches.cn: 日常损失与仪式供奉共享同一动作。

intro.en: Sacrifice joins Latin sacer (holy) and facere (to make).
intro.cn: sacrifice 由拉丁语 sacer（神圣）与 facere（做）组合。

latinIntro.en: Latin sacer, facere, and sacrificium are the source forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sacer、facere 与 sacrificium 是来源词形。

items.example: Facere means to perform a rite.

definition_zh: 悲伤的；难过的；令人难过的；可悲的
definition_en: feeling unhappy; showing sorrow; making people feel unhappy; unfortunate and regrettable
core_image: 低着头、眼角含泪的一张脸
scene: 听到那个消息后，她显得很悲伤。She looked sad after hearing the news.
sceneCN: 这里 sad 是「悲伤的、难过的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：听到那个消息后，她显得很悲伤。

pos.zh: 令人难过的；令人悲伤的

senses.title: Feeling unhappy
senses.definition: feeling unhappy because something painful has happened
senses.definitionCN: 因发生痛苦的事而感到不快乐的
senses.example: She looked sad when she heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息时，她显得很悲伤。
senses.why: The core sense is low spirits inside a person.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是人内心低落的情绪。

senses.title: Causing sorrow
senses.titleCN: 令人难过的；令人悲伤的
senses.definition: making people feel unhappy or full of sorrow
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到不快或充满悲伤的
senses.example: It was a sad story about a lost child.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一个关于走失孩子的悲伤故事。
senses.why: The feeling spreads from people to what causes it.
senses.whyCN: 情绪从人扩展到引起情绪的事物。

senses.title: Regrettable
senses.definition: unfortunate and disappointing in a way that brings sorrow
senses.definitionCN: 不幸且令人失望、使人感到悲伤的
senses.example: It is sad that so many people were left out.
senses.exampleCN: 这么多人被排除在外，实在令人遗憾。
senses.why: Sorrow becomes a judgment on a situation.
senses.whyCN: 悲伤转为对某种处境的评判。

intro.en: Sad comes from Old English sæd, which first meant sated or weary.
intro.cn: sad 源自古英语 sæd，最初意为「吃饱的、疲倦的」。

items.en: Sæd means sated or weary.
items.cn: 古英语 sæd 意为吃饱的或疲倦的。

items.en: Fullness turns into weariness of spirit.
items.cn: 「饱足」引申为精神上的厌倦。

items.en: Sad comes to mean sorrowful.
items.cn: 中古英语中 sad 转为「悲伤的」。

items.en: Sad settles as the common word for sorrow.
items.cn: 近代早期英语中 sad 固定为表示悲伤的常用词。

items.en: Sad describes people, news, and situations.
items.cn: 现代英语中 sad 可形容人、消息与处境。

note.en: Sad means sorrowful; said is the past of say.
note.cn: sad 是悲伤的，said 则是 say 的过去式。

normalIntro.en: Sad appears whenever something painful or disappointing happens.
normalIntro.cn: 当痛苦或失望的事情发生时，就会用到 sad。

normal.en: She felt sad when her friend moved away.
normal.cn: 朋友搬走时，她感到很难过。

normal.en: The film has a sad ending.
normal.cn: 这部电影有一个悲伤的结局。

normal.en: He gave a sad smile and said nothing.
normal.cn: 他悲伤地笑了笑，什么也没说。

normal.en: It is sad to see the old shop close.
normal.cn: 看到老店关门，令人难过。

normal.en: The letter brought sad news from home.
normal.cn: 这封信带来了家里的悲伤消息。

abstract.en: Picture a face with lowered eyes and a heavy heart.
abstract.cn: 想象一张低垂双眼、心情沉重的脸。

abstract.en: Imagine rain falling on an empty playground.
abstract.cn: 想象雨落在空无一人的操场上。

abstract.en: Think of a song that slows down at the end.
abstract.cn: 想象一首在结尾放慢的歌曲。

examples.en: She was sad to leave her childhood home.
examples.cn: 离开童年的家让她很难过。

examples.en: The sad news spread through the village.
examples.cn: 这个令人难过的消息传遍了村庄。

examples.en: It is sad that the concert was cancelled.
examples.cn: 音乐会被取消，实在令人遗憾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sad」谐音「散的」：曲终人散，心里难免悲伤。

root: 源自古英语 sæd（吃饱的、厌倦的），由「饱足而生倦」引申为「心情低落、悲伤」。

sensesIntro.en: Sad means feeling unhappy, causing sorrow, or being unfortunate and regrettable.
sensesIntro.cn: sad 意为感到不快、令人悲伤的，或不幸而令人遗憾的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face lowered by sorrow.
core.cn: 核心意象：因悲伤而低垂的一张脸。

branches.en: The base sense is inner unhappiness.
branches.cn: 基础义是内心的不快。

branches.en: Feeling spreads to what causes it.
branches.cn: 情绪扩展到引起它的对象。

branches.en: Sorrow becomes a judgment on events.
branches.cn: 悲伤转为对事件的评判。

branches.en: A person and a story can both be sad.
branches.cn: 人与故事都可以是悲伤的。

branches.en: Sad news and a sad outcome overlap.
branches.cn: 悲伤的消息与可悲的结果相互重叠。

intro.en: Sad is a Germanic word that builds a small family with -ly, -ness, and -en.
intro.cn: sad 是日耳曼语词，通过 -ly、-ness 与 -en 构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Sad has no Latin root; it comes from Old English sæd.
latinIntro.cn: sad 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 sæd。

items.example: She spoke sadly about the past.

items.exampleCN: 这个消息让大家很悲伤。
一只眼神悲伤的狗在外面等候。
那位面带悲伤的男子什么也没说。

definition_zh: 马鞍；给马备鞍；使承担（负担、债务）
definition_en: a seat for a rider on a horse; to put a saddle on a horse; to make someone carry a burden
core_image: 搭在马背上、带脚镫的皮制坐垫
scene: 天亮前，他给马备好了鞍。He saddled the horse before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 saddle 是「给马备鞍」（第 2 个义项）；句意：天亮前，他给马备好了鞍。

senses.title: Rider's seat
senses.definition: a leather seat fastened on a horse for a rider
senses.definitionCN: 固定在马背上供骑手乘坐的皮制坐垫
senses.example: He tightened the saddle before riding.
senses.exampleCN: 骑行前，他把马鞍系紧。
senses.why: The core object is the seat on a horse.
senses.whyCN: 核心物件是马背上的座位。

senses.title: Put on a saddle
senses.definition: to put a saddle on a horse
senses.example: She saddled the pony quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 她很快给小马备好了鞍。
senses.why: The object turns into the action of fitting it.
senses.whyCN: 名词物件转为安装它的动作。

senses.title: Burden someone
senses.definition: to make someone carry a duty, debt, or problem
senses.definitionCN: 使某人承担职责、债务或问题
senses.example: The new rules saddled small firms with extra costs.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定让小企业承担了额外成本。
senses.why: A load on a horse becomes a burden on a person.
senses.whyCN: 马背上的重物变成人身上的负担。

intro.en: Saddle comes from Old English sadol, a word linked to the idea of sitting.
intro.cn: saddle 源自古英语 sadol，这个词与「坐」的概念有关。

items.en: Sadol names the rider's seat.
items.cn: sadol 指骑手乘坐的座位。

items.en: The word is linked to the idea of sitting.
items.cn: 这个词与「坐」的概念相关联。

items.en: Saddle keeps both seat and horse gear.
items.cn: saddle 同时保留座位与马具两层意思。

items.en: To saddle grows the sense of loading.
items.cn: 动词 saddle 发展出「装载」的含义。

items.en: Saddle also means to burden with duty or debt.
items.cn: saddle 也可表示使人承担职责或债务。

note.en: Saddle is horse gear; straddle is to sit across something.
note.cn: saddle 是马具，straddle 则是跨坐。

entries.definition: a short oar used to move a small boat
to sit with legs on both sides
to end a dispute or arrange a place
to give someone a heavy duty

normalIntro.en: Saddle names the rider's seat and the act of fitting it.
normalIntro.cn: saddle 既指骑手乘坐的马鞍，也指把马鞍装上的动作。

normal.en: The rider checked the saddle before setting off.
normal.cn: 骑手出发前检查了马鞍。

normal.en: He learned to saddle a horse at the farm.
normal.cn: 他在农场学会了给马备鞍。

normal.en: The old saddle was worn and cracked.
normal.cn: 那只旧马鞍又破又裂。

normal.en: New taxes saddled the family with debt.
normal.cn: 新税让这个家庭背上了债务。

normal.en: She stayed in the saddle all afternoon.
normal.cn: 她整个下午都骑在马背上。

abstract.en: Picture a leather seat resting on a horse's back.
abstract.cn: 想象一只皮制坐垫搭在马背上。

abstract.en: Imagine a heavy bag tied behind the rider.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉重的袋子绑在骑手身后。

abstract.en: Think of a worker carrying a load that is not his own.
abstract.cn: 想象一名工人背着并不属于他的重担。

examples.en: The saddle slipped as the horse turned.
examples.cn: 马转弯时，马鞍滑动了。

examples.en: They saddled the horses before sunrise.
examples.cn: 他们在日出前给马备好了鞍。

examples.en: The policy saddled farmers with new paperwork.
examples.cn: 这项政策让农民承担了新的文书工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「saddle」谐音「赛斗」：赛马之前，先给马备好马鞍。

root: 源自古英语 sadol（马鞍），与「坐」的概念相关；由马背上的座位引申出「备鞍」与「使人承担负担」。

sensesIntro.en: Saddle means the rider's seat, the act of putting it on a horse, or making someone carry a burden.
sensesIntro.cn: saddle 意为马鞍、给马备鞍，或使某人承担负担。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a leather seat on a horse's back.
core.cn: 核心意象：马背上的皮制坐垫。

branches.en: The base sense is the seat for a rider.
branches.cn: 基础义是供骑手乘坐的马鞍。

branches.en: The object becomes the action of fitting it.
branches.cn: 名词物件转为安装它的动作。

branches.en: A load on an animal becomes a human burden.
branches.cn: 动物背上的重物变成人的负担。

branches.en: The seat and the act of placing it belong together.
branches.cn: 马鞍与安装马鞍的动作相互关联。

branches.en: Fitting gear and imposing a duty share the idea of loading.
branches.cn: 装备马具与施加职责都带有「装载」之意。

intro.en: Saddle comes from an Old English root linked to sitting, with a family that includes saddler and saddlery.
intro.cn: saddle 的古英语词根与「坐」有关，词族包括 saddler 与 saddlery。

latinIntro.en: Saddle has no Latin root; Latin sella meaning seat is only a distant semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: saddle 没有拉丁词根；拉丁语 sella（座椅）只是意义相近的旁证。

items.meaning: horse seat or to fit one
items.example: He put the saddle on the horse.

items.meaning: fitted with a saddle or burdened
items.example: The horse was saddled and ready.
items.exampleCN: 马已备好鞍，随时可以出发。

items.meaning: the act of fitting a saddle

items.example: The saddler repaired the old leather.
The saddlery smells of oil and leather.
items.exampleCN: 马具店里弥漫着油和皮革的气味。

items.meaning: a bag attached to a saddle
items.example: He packed food in his saddlebag.

items.meaning: a saddle for riding with both legs on one side
items.example: She rode sidesaddle along the lane.
items.exampleCN: 她侧坐在马鞍上沿小路骑行。

items.example: They unsaddled the horses at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 黄昏时他们卸下了马鞍。

definition_en: in a sad way; in a way that shows regret; unfortunately
core_image: 低声说话、缓缓摇头的悲伤神情
scene: 她悲伤地摇了摇头。She shook her head sadly.
sceneCN: 这里 sadly 是「悲伤地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她悲伤地摇了摇头。

senses.title: In a sad way
senses.definition: with feelings of sorrow or unhappiness
senses.definitionCN: 带着悲伤或不快的情绪
senses.example: She looked sadly at the old photograph.
senses.exampleCN: 她悲伤地看着那张旧照片。
senses.why: The suffix -ly turns the feeling into a manner.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ly 把情绪转成做事的方式。

senses.title: With regret
senses.definition: with a feeling of disappointment or regret
senses.definitionCN: 带着失望或遗憾的心情
senses.example: Sadly, the train had already left.
senses.exampleCN: 遗憾的是，火车已经开走了。
senses.why: Regret colors the speaker's comment on a fact.
senses.whyCN: 遗憾给说话人对事实的评论染上色彩。

senses.title: Unfortunately
senses.definition: used to say that something is unfortunate
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事不幸或令人惋惜
senses.example: Sadly, many families lost their homes.
senses.exampleCN: 不幸的是，许多家庭失去了家园。
senses.why: The sentence adverb marks bad news.
senses.whyCN: 句子副词用来标记坏消息。

intro.en: Sadly is sad plus the adverb ending -ly, from Old English -lice.
intro.cn: sadly 由 sad 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，-ly 源自古英语 -lice。

items.en: The ending -lice forms adverbs of manner.
items.cn: 古英语词尾 -lice 构成方式副词。

items.en: The ending becomes -ly in everyday use.
items.cn: 中古英语中该词尾在日常使用中变为 -ly。

items.en: Sadly describes how someone speaks or moves.
items.cn: sadly 描述某人说话或动作的方式。

items.en: Sadly also comments on unfortunate facts.
items.cn: sadly 也可评述不幸的事实。

items.en: The pattern is adjective plus -ly.
items.cn: 构词模式是形容词加 -ly。

note.en: Sadly means with sorrow; badly means in a poor way.
note.cn: sadly 是悲伤地，badly 则是糟糕地。

entries.definition: in a poor or harmful way
in a wild or very eager way
by bad luck or in a sad way

normalIntro.en: Sadly tells how something is done or comments on bad news.
normalIntro.cn: sadly 既说明事情如何发生，也可用来评论坏消息。

normal.en: She smiled sadly and closed the door.
normal.cn: 她悲伤地笑了笑，关上了门。

normal.en: He spoke sadly about his old school.
normal.cn: 他悲伤地谈起自己的母校。

normal.en: Sadly, the concert was cancelled.
normal.cn: 遗憾的是，音乐会被取消了。

normal.en: The dog waited sadly by the gate.
normal.cn: 狗悲伤地在门边等候。

normal.en: Sadly, few people came to the meeting.
normal.cn: 不幸的是，来开会的人很少。

abstract.en: Picture a person speaking in a low, slow voice.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人用低沉缓慢的声音说话。

abstract.en: Imagine a head shaking slowly from side to side.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗头缓缓地左右摇动。

abstract.en: Think of a sigh that comes before bad news.
abstract.cn: 想象坏消息到来前的一声叹息。

examples.en: She looked sadly at the empty chair.
examples.cn: 她悲伤地看着那把空椅子。

examples.en: Sadly, the museum closed last year.
examples.cn: 遗憾的是，博物馆去年关闭了。

examples.en: He smiled sadly and said goodbye.
examples.cn: 他悲伤地微笑着道别。

dict_mnemonic.text: sad 加副词后缀 -ly，表示「以悲伤的方式」，就是 sadly。

root: 由形容词 sad 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，核心义「以悲伤或遗憾的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: Sadly means in a sorrowful manner, with regret, or unfortunately.
sensesIntro.cn: sadly 意为以悲伤的方式、带着遗憾，或不幸地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sorrowful voice and a slow shake of the head.
core.cn: 核心意象：悲伤的嗓音与缓慢的摇头。

branches.en: The base sense is the manner of sorrow.
branches.cn: 基础义是带悲伤的行为方式。

branches.en: Disappointment adds a tone of regret.
branches.cn: 失望为语气添上遗憾。

branches.en: The adverb comments on an unfortunate fact.
branches.cn: 副词用来评述不幸的事实。

branches.en: Sorrowful manner and regretful tone overlap.
branches.cn: 悲伤的方式与遗憾的语气相互重叠。

branches.en: Regret and bad news often appear together.
branches.cn: 遗憾与坏消息常常同时出现。

intro.en: Sadly is built from sad plus the native English adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: sadly 由 sad 加英语本族副词词尾 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: Sadly has no Latin root; its ending descends from Old English -lice.
latinIntro.cn: sadly 没有拉丁词根，其词尾来自古英语 -lice。

items.example: Her sadness was easy to see.
items.exampleCN: 她的悲伤很容易看出来。
这个故事让孩子们很悲伤。
那个眼神悲伤的女孩独自等候。

items.example: A sad-faced officer read the letter.
items.exampleCN: 一位面带悲伤的官员读了那封信。

definition_zh: 悲伤；难过；令人悲伤的事
definition_en: the feeling of being sad; the quality of showing sorrow; a sad event or fact
core_image: 胸口发沉、眼泪将落未落的感觉
scene: 她眼中流露出深深的悲伤。There was deep sadness in her eyes.
sceneCN: 这里 sadness 是「悲伤、难过」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她眼中流露出深深的悲伤。

senses.title: The feeling of sorrow
senses.definition: the feeling of being unhappy and sorrowful
senses.definitionCN: 不快乐而又悲伤的感受
senses.example: A wave of sadness washed over him.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵悲伤涌上他的心头。
senses.why: The core sense is the inner state of sorrow.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是内心悲伤的状态。

senses.title: Outward sign of sorrow
senses.definition: the quality of looking or sounding sorrowful
senses.definitionCN: 神情或声音中流露出的悲伤
senses.example: There was sadness in her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的声音里带着悲伤。
senses.why: The inner state becomes visible to others.
senses.whyCN: 内心的状态变得让旁人看得见。

senses.title: A sad fact
senses.definition: something that makes people feel sorrow
senses.example: The sadness of the story stayed with me.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事的悲伤一直留在我心里。
senses.why: A state becomes a fact that can be named.
senses.whyCN: 状态变成可以被指称的事实。

intro.en: Sadness is sad plus the noun ending -ness, from Old English -nes.
intro.cn: sadness 由 sad 加名词词尾 -ness 构成，-ness 源自古英语 -nes。

items.en: The ending -nes forms nouns of state.
items.cn: 古英语词尾 -nes 构成表示状态的名词。

items.en: Sad still carries the sense of weary fullness.
items.cn: 当时的 sad 仍带有「饱足而倦」的含义。

items.en: Sadness names the state of being sorrowful.
items.cn: sadness 指悲伤的状态。

items.en: The word appears in poetry and letters.
items.cn: 这个词出现在诗歌与书信中。

items.en: Sadness covers feelings, signs, and sad facts.
items.cn: sadness 涵盖感受、表现与令人悲伤的事实。

note.en: Sadness is the state; sorrow is its deeper form.
note.cn: sadness 是悲伤的状态，sorrow 则是更深的悲痛。

normalIntro.en: Sadness names the feeling of sorrow and the signs it leaves.
normalIntro.cn: sadness 指悲伤的感受，也指它留下的种种表现。

normal.en: A deep sadness filled the empty house.
normal.cn: 深深的悲伤充满了空荡的房子。

normal.en: She could not hide her sadness.
normal.cn: 她无法掩饰自己的悲伤。

normal.en: There was sadness in his quiet voice.
normal.cn: 他平静的声音里带着悲伤。

normal.en: The sadness of the ending surprised us.
normal.cn: 结局的悲伤让我们感到意外。

normal.en: Music can express sadness without words.
normal.cn: 音乐可以不用语言表达悲伤。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy weight resting on the chest.
abstract.cn: 想象胸口压着一块沉重的石头。

abstract.en: Imagine tears that stop before they fall.
abstract.cn: 想象泪水将落未落。

abstract.en: Think of an empty room after a farewell.
abstract.cn: 想象告别之后空荡的房间。

examples.en: His sadness was clear to everyone.
examples.cn: 他的悲伤大家都看得出来。

examples.en: She wrote a poem about loss and sadness.
examples.cn: 她写了一首关于失去与悲伤的诗。

examples.en: The sadness of the news spread across the town.
examples.cn: 这个消息带来的悲伤传遍了小镇。

dict_mnemonic.text: sad 加名词后缀 -ness，表示「悲伤的状态」，就是 sadness。

root: 由形容词 sad 加名词词尾 -ness 构成，核心义「悲伤的状态及其表现」。

sensesIntro.en: Sadness means the feeling of sorrow, its outward signs, or a sad fact.
sensesIntro.cn: sadness 意为悲伤的感受、悲伤的表现，或令人悲伤的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy feeling behind the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：双眼里沉甸甸的感受。

branches.en: The base sense is the inner feeling.
branches.cn: 基础义是内心的感受。

branches.en: Feeling becomes visible in face and voice.
branches.cn: 感受在神情与声音中显现。

branches.en: Sorrow becomes a fact that can be named.
branches.cn: 悲伤变成可以被指称的事实。

branches.en: Inner sorrow and outward grief belong together.
branches.cn: 内心的悲伤与外在的哀伤相互关联。

branches.en: Visible grief and sad events often overlap.
branches.cn: 可见的哀伤与悲伤的事件常常重叠。

intro.en: Sadness is sad plus -ness, one of the most productive noun endings in English.
intro.cn: sadness 由 sad 加 -ness 构成，-ness 是英语中构词力很强的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Sadness has no Latin root; both sad and -ness are native English elements.
latinIntro.cn: sadness 没有拉丁词根；sad 与 -ness 都是英语本族成分。

items.exampleCN: 这个消息让全家很悲伤。

items.example: The room felt sadder at night.
It was the saddest day of the year.
items.exampleCN: 那是一年中最悲伤的一天。

items.example: A sad-eyed child stood at the door.
items.exampleCN: 一个眼神悲伤的孩子站在门口。
那位面带悲伤的女士向我们道谢。

definition_zh: 安全的；未受伤害的；稳妥的；保险箱
definition_en: free from danger; not harmed; likely to be right; a strong box for valuables
core_image: 一扇锁好的金属保险箱和一把钥匙
scene: 她把文件锁进了保险箱。She locked the documents in the safe.
sceneCN: 这里 safe 是「保险箱」（第 4 个义项）；句意：她把文件锁进了保险箱。

pos.zh: 未受伤害的；安然无恙的

senses.title: Free from danger
senses.definition: not likely to be harmed or damaged
senses.definitionCN: 不太可能受到伤害或损坏的
senses.example: Keep the medicine in a safe place.
senses.exampleCN: 把药放在安全的地方。
senses.why: The core sense is protection from danger.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是免于危险。

senses.title: Not harmed
senses.titleCN: 未受伤害的；安然无恙的
senses.definition: unharmed after a danger or accident
senses.definitionCN: 经历危险或事故后没有受伤的
senses.example: The children were found safe after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后，孩子们被找到时安然无恙。
senses.why: Protection produces the result of being unharmed.
senses.whyCN: 保护带来未受伤害的结果。

senses.title: Reliable
senses.definition: likely to be correct or to succeed
senses.example: It is a safe bet that prices will rise.
senses.exampleCN: 价格上涨是很有把握的。
senses.why: Physical security becomes confidence in a choice.
senses.whyCN: 身体的安全转为对选择的信心。

senses.title: Strong box
senses.definition: a strong metal box for keeping valuables
senses.definitionCN: 用来存放贵重物品的坚固金属箱
senses.example: The hotel offers a safe in every room.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店的每个房间都配有保险箱。
senses.why: Protection becomes a container for valuables.
senses.whyCN: 保护变成存放贵重物品的容器。

intro.en: Safe comes from Latin salvus, meaning uninjured or healthy, through Old French sauf.
intro.cn: safe 经由古法语 sauf 来自拉丁语 salvus，意为「未受伤的、健康的」。

items.en: Salvus means uninjured and healthy.
items.cn: salvus 意为未受伤的、健康的。

items.en: Salus means health and safety.
items.cn: salus 意为健康与安全。

items.en: Sauf carries the sense of being unharmed.
items.cn: sauf 保留「未受伤害」的含义。

items.en: Safe means secure from harm.
items.cn: 中古英语中 safe 意为免受伤害。

items.en: Safe also names a strong box.
items.cn: 现代英语中 safe 也指保险箱。

note.en: Safe means protected; save means to rescue.
note.cn: safe 是安全的，save 则是拯救。

normalIntro.en: Safe covers freedom from danger, the result of being unharmed, and a strong box.
normalIntro.cn: safe 涵盖免于危险、未受伤害的结果，以及保险箱。

normal.en: Keep your passport in a safe place.
normal.cn: 把护照放在安全的地方。

normal.en: The missing climbers were found safe.
normal.cn: 失踪的登山者被找到时安然无恙。

normal.en: It is safer to travel by day.
normal.cn: 白天出行更安全。

normal.en: The shop keeps its cash in a safe.
normal.cn: 这家店把现金放在保险箱里。

normal.en: We wish you a safe journey home.
normal.cn: 祝你回家一路平安。

abstract.en: Picture a locked metal box with a heavy door.
abstract.cn: 想象一只锁好的金属箱，箱门厚重。

abstract.en: Imagine a child returning unharmed from a storm.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子经历暴风雨后安然归来。

abstract.en: Think of a bridge that holds firm under weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一座在重压下依然稳固的桥。

examples.en: The old documents are kept in a safe.
examples.cn: 旧文件保存在保险箱里。

examples.en: Make sure the children are safe.
examples.cn: 确保孩子们安全。

examples.en: It is a safe choice for a first job.
examples.cn: 对第一份工作来说，这是个稳妥的选择。

dict_mnemonic.text: safe 与 save 只差一个字母：先 save（拯救），才有 safe（安全）。

root: 源自拉丁语 salvus（未受伤的、健康的），经古法语 sauf 进入英语，核心义「免受伤害、处于安全之中」。

sensesIntro.en: Safe means free from danger, unharmed, reliable, or a strong box.
sensesIntro.cn: safe 意为没有危险的、未受伤害的、稳妥可靠的，或保险箱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a locked strong box and a key.
core.cn: 核心意象：锁好的坚固箱子与一把钥匙。

branches.en: The base sense is freedom from danger.
branches.cn: 基础义是免于危险。

branches.en: Protection yields the result of being unharmed.
branches.cn: 保护带来未受伤害的结果。

branches.en: Security becomes confidence in a choice.
branches.cn: 安全转为对选择的信心。

branches.en: Protection becomes a metal container.
branches.cn: 保护变成一只金属容器。

branches.en: Danger avoided and harm escaped overlap.
branches.cn: 避开危险与逃过伤害相互重叠。

intro.en: Safe comes from Latin salvus and builds a family with safety, safely, and safeguard.
intro.cn: safe 来自拉丁语 salvus，并构成 safety、safely 与 safeguard 等词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin salvus and salus are the distant sources of safe and safety.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 salvus 与 salus 是 safe 与 safety 的远源。

items.example: The money is in the safe.
They tested the safeness of the water.
items.exampleCN: 他们检测了水的安全性。

items.example: This route is safer at night.
items.exampleCN: 这条路线在夜里更安全。

items.example: It is the safest place to wait.
items.exampleCN: 这是最安全的等候地点。

items.example: The bridge is unsafe after the flood.
items.exampleCN: 洪水过后这座桥不安全。

items.meaning: a person who opens safes illegally
items.example: The safecracker was caught at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 撬保险箱的盗贼在黎明时被抓。

latinEntries.example: Salvus gives the core sense of safe.
latinEntries.exampleCN: salvus 提供 safe 的核心含义。

latinEntries.example: Salus is the source of safety.
latinEntries.exampleCN: salus 是 safety 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Salvare is related to being safe.
latinEntries.exampleCN: salvare 与「安全」这一概念相关。
